correctness.rationale: The exact orthonormal tensor-cube Fourier-character family has isotropic derivative energy. Sharp equality forces all functions into the uniquely lowest N Fourier modes; the odd-t periodic parity class is strictly excluded. Each constant-modulus finite Fourier polynomial is one monomial by its extreme autocorrelation coefficient. Adjacent cube-index ratios make the lifted curve affine with integer winding, and distinct consecutive digit sums force the winding magnitudes to equal powers of t+1. The converse follows from repeated reduction modulo t+1. The actual standalone exact-integer checker passed 13 parameter cases covering 545 lattice points of the matching Euclidean norm; computation is only diagnostic for the analytical proof.

originality.rationale: Ehler proves the sharp lower bound and provides Korobov minimizers; an all-rectifiable-curves equality classification is not stated in the inspected paper. Kunis gives constructive periodic straight-line quadratures and quasi-optimality, not uniqueness. The further strict spectral-support, unimodular-Laurent and radix-weight argument is needed to force any minimizer to be a signed/permuted Korobov geodesic. No equivalent or stronger claim appeared in the actual published-finding corpus or web searches; literature incompleteness is a residual risk.
residual_risks: Ehler refers to Korobov curves as equality cases; an unstated conventional assertion of uniqueness might appear in a source not indexed under these terms.

value.rationale: The exact minimum in an infinite-dimensional class of closed rectifiable box-Fourier design curves does not by itself characterize all equality curves. Excluding every nonlinear extremizer and every non-Korobov winding vector is a natural structural rigidity/inverse problem: it determines the entire optimal path geometry and admissible winding classes. It is not a numerical one-off or a routine exponent change. The scope is precisely equality, with no unsupported quantitative stability result.
